bug_semantics: A course student can bypass navigation/button hiding by directly loading /courses/{course-id}/settings#share or /courses/{course-id}/people?add=true. The settings route renders course-management settings without a route-level student-role guard, while the people invitation modal derives its open state from the user-controlled add=true query even though the ordinary Add button is role-gated. This is an object-keyed authorization failure, not merely hidden UI discoverability.
flaw_origin: The earliest disclosed surface is the unguarded settings route. It first appears in the public history at one-parent Space merge boundary 103a2eda7b039f6ee1fb9ea524c41b0a85fe158e, whose message aggregates numerous CLASSROOMIO-T-90/T-14x member commits and whose parent lacks the settings route. Because that boundary is a squash aggregate and none of its original CLASSROOMIO-T-90 member commit objects is present, the smallest real settings BIC cannot be named. The later invite-query surface is independently decomposable: 0b61becdbe1e5d4f7c5d03a3819ff4e0b6792d1a, not its parent 9f04d4e3a7dd3335ea8fc7db10efe78eab1431a7, first makes add=true itself open the modal; that later BIC cannot replace the unavailable earlier BIC for the advisory's combined vulnerability.
ai_marker: unknown: the true member BIC that first added the unguarded settings route is absent, so its commit-object author, committer, message, and trailers cannot be inspected. Public aggregate 103a2eda7b039f6ee1fb9ea524c41b0a85fe158e has human co-authors and no AI marker, but aggregate metadata is inadmissible; later invite BIC 0b61becdbe1e5d4f7c5d03a3819ff4e0b6792d1a likewise has no AI marker but is not the earliest case BIC.
evidence: Disagreement resolution for verdict and introducer_sha: the primary selected later invite member 0b61becdbe1e5d4f7c5d03a3819ff4e0b6792d1a and NOT_AI, while the reviewer selected BLOCKED with a null introducer because the earlier settings origin is an undecomposed aggregate. `git log --all --reverse --format='%H %P %s' -- <all settings-route paths>` places the settings route first at the three rebased copies eec1c1ab8a6594bb948c050136303abe20183abb, caa5b2f804d0377ba483fd73e51d3b4ca902df11, and mainline 103a2eda7b039f6ee1fb9ea524c41b0a85fe158e; `git show --no-patch --format='%H %T %P %aI %s'` proves all three have identical tree 841f3881a14a082d6460b9c8183e1fafcc79ded8 and the same timestamp/subject but different single parents. The advisory bundle names both the settings and invite paths, so narrowing the case to the later invite path is invalid. The reviewer's BLOCKED/null conclusion wins, although one invite-side claim was wrong as detailed below.

Aggregate rejection and missing-member boundary: `git cat-file -p 103a2eda7b039f6ee1fb9ea524c41b0a85fe158e` shows one parent, Space Cloud as committer, `Merge-request: CLASSROOMIO-MR-76`, and a message concatenating numerous CLASSROOMIO-T-90/T-14x subjects and merge commits. A `git cat-file --batch-all-objects` scan inspected all 5,721 commit objects: every embedded CLASSROOMIO-T-90 subject was absent as a commit-object subject except `CLASSROOMIO-T-90:Implemented the course settings`, which existed only as the three aggregate copies 103a2eda7b039f6ee1fb9ea524c41b0a85fe158e, caa5b2f804d0377ba483fd73e51d3b4ca902df11, and eec1c1ab8a6594bb948c050136303abe20183abb. Thus no true member BIC object is available and squash_decomposed remains false.

Disagreement resolution for introducer_parent and parent_absence: `git cat-file -p 103a2eda7b039f6ee1fb9ea524c41b0a85fe158e` gives public-boundary parent e44353ac0a429694405e0b13494c6041d842bcb1; `git ls-tree -r --name-only e44353ac0a429694405e0b13494c6041d842bcb1 -- 'src/routes/courses/[id]/settings'` is empty, and `git diff --name-status e44353ac0a429694405e0b13494c6041d842bcb1 103a2eda7b039f6ee1fb9ea524c41b0a85fe158e -- 'src/routes/courses/[id]/settings'` reports +page.js and +page.svelte added. This proves absence at the aggregate boundary only. Because 103a2eda7b039f6ee1fb9ea524c41b0a85fe158e is rejected as a BIC, e44353ac0a429694405e0b13494c6041d842bcb1 is not the unknown true BIC's immediate parent; introducer_parent must be null and introducer_parent_absent false. The primary's 9f04d4e3a7dd3335ea8fc7db10efe78eab1431a7 parent applies only to the later invite BIC.

Vulnerable settings mechanism at the public boundary: `git grep` at 103a2eda7b039f6ee1fb9ea524c41b0a85fe158e finds `isStudent = user.role_id === 3` in CourseContainer, `return !isStudent` in Navigation, but unconditional `<slot />` in CourseContainer; the newly added settings/+page.svelte wraps and renders Settings through that container without a route authorization check. Hiding the Settings navigation item therefore does not prevent a direct settings URL.

Invite-side correction: contrary to the reviewer's claim that 9f04d4e3a7dd3335ea8fc7db10efe78eab1431a7 opened the modal on direct navigation, `git show 9f04d4e3...` shows checkQueryParamAndOpenModal() called only by handleClick(), and that handler remains on the Add button inside RoleBasedSecurity. `git grep` at 9f04d4e3 finds no addPeopleParm and shows the modal still uses `bind:open={$invitationModal.open}`. `git show 0b61becdbe1e5d4f7c5d03a3819ff4e0b6792d1a` first adds reactive query parsing and `open={addPeopleParm === 'true'}`; `git rev-parse 0b61becd...^` returns 9f04d4e3a7dd3335ea8fc7db10efe78eab1431a7. The primary was correct about this later surface and its direct parent, but wrong to promote it over the earlier settings origin.

BIC-only AI check: `git cat-file -p 0b61becdbe1e5d4f7c5d03a3819ff4e0b6792d1a` records human author/committer tunny17, parent 9f04d4e3a7dd3335ea8fc7db10efe78eab1431a7, message `code refactor`, and no trailers; `git cat-file -p 103a2eda7b039f6ee1fb9ea524c41b0a85fe158e` likewise has no AI marker but is the rejected aggregate. Neither object can establish AI attribution for the absent true settings member BIC, so NOT_AI is not gate-complete.

Affected version boundary: the bundled GHSA-px6j-wc84-gwhf/CVE-2025-65672 advisory identifies ClassroomIO 0.1.13 and both direct-access surfaces. `git rev-parse v0.1.13^{}` returns 876a785b3c467b809804f56e0981bff448fcfdb5; `git merge-base --is-ancestor 103a2eda7b039f6ee1fb9ea524c41b0a85fe158e v0.1.13` and the same check against v0.1.0 both succeed. At v0.1.13, `git grep` finds Settings rendered at settings/+page.svelte:13, `query.get('add')` at InvitationModal.svelte:179, and `open={addPeopleParm === 'true'}` at line 188.

Unpatched boundary: `git rev-parse origin/main` returns f08f6c6838259ca440299a82f5d100d44d5349cd. At that exact tip, `git grep` finds invitation modal `isOpen` derived solely from `addPeopleParm === 'true'` at line 33, CourseSettingsPage rendered by the settings route at line 41, and the shared course layout admitting `$isOrgAdmin || user` at line 92. The vulnerable paths therefore remain in the validated tip; no fix or patched-version boundary exists, so fix_sha and direct_fix_sha are null for an explicitly unpatched case rather than for an unsearched fix.

Invitation squash context does not cure the earlier gap: `git cat-file -p 82eee93417616e4dce0cec9ef30a988da07231c9` lists members `feat add`, `code refactor`, and `Update +page.svelte`; the recoverable member chain includes 9f04d4e3a7dd3335ea8fc7db10efe78eab1431a7 and 0b61becdbe1e5d4f7c5d03a3819ff4e0b6792d1a. That decomposition establishes the later invite BIC but cannot decompose the earlier Space settings squash or supply its BIC commit object.
reasoning: The primary and reviewer disagreed because the primary treated the advisory's query-controlled invitation modal as the decisive origin, while the reviewer treated the earlier unguarded settings route as part of the same disclosed authorization flaw. The latter scope is correct: the bundle explicitly identifies unauthorized share and invite access, and both paths implement the same UI-only authorization mistake. History independently proves that 0b61becdbe1e5d4f7c5d03a3819ff4e0b6792d1a is the smallest invite-query BIC and that its immediate parent lacks direct-query opening, correcting the reviewer's mistaken attribution to 9f04d4e3a7dd3335ea8fc7db10efe78eab1431a7. But the settings exposure predates that invite change and landed through 103a2eda7b039f6ee1fb9ea524c41b0a85fe158e, an aggregate that the protocol forbids using as a BIC. Its parent proves only aggregate-boundary absence; the unavailable true member BIC and its immediate parent require introducer_sha and introducer_parent to be null and parent_absence to remain unproven/false. Because AI evidence is admissible only from that missing true BIC object, neither the human-looking aggregate nor the later human-authored invite BIC supports NOT_AI. The vulnerability and affected/unpatched boundaries are established, but attribution is blocked, yielding BLOCKED.
remaining_gap: The original JetBrains Space CLASSROOMIO-MR-76 member commit object that first wrote the unguarded settings route, and therefore its immediate parent and BIC-only AI metadata, is absent from all 5,721 commit objects in the validated clone. The public aggregate boundary proves the route was absent before the squash but cannot substitute for those objects. The flaw itself is explicitly unpatched through origin/main f08f6c6838259ca440299a82f5d100d44d5349cd; only causal/AI attribution remains blocked.
